findings.claim: The Safe address book no longer offers a rows-per-page picker (10 / 25 / 100) and always shows 25 rows, which is a regression compared to the previous table; this is a visible feature loss for users with many contacts who now must page through more pages to see the same number of entries.

The 'Requested' and 'Already shared' labels use an aria-label on a plain span with no role, and the icons themselves are hidden from screen readers, so most screen readers will skip these labels; the existing test passes only because the testing library accepts the label regardless of accessibility semantics, masking the real issue.
The same aria-label-on-plain-span issue affects this location, meaning a screen-reader user on a narrow screen would hear nothing for these rows.

The action buttons reuse the old table's .actions CSS class, which switches to justify-content: flex-start below 900px while the header stays right-aligned, causing the buttons to be misaligned under the header on narrow screens including phones, which previously used a separate mobile card layout.
A comment was truncated during the diff, cutting off mid-sentence at 'almost touching' after the line 'the table card below it' was deleted; the comment should be restored.
The doc comment still states 'nine existing consumers' but after removing the address book there are now only eight consumers, so the count is out of date.

No unit tests cover the new narrow-screen layout of the Safe address book (address appearing under the name, address column being dropped) or sorting by address, so a regression in the compact/narrow-screen behavior would not be caught by unit tests even though Cypress covers the sorting behavior.

The Safe address book's own 'address under the name' cell duplicates the new AddressCell component, but AddressCell lives in the Spaces feature, which a shared component should not import from; moving AddressCell to components/common would let both features share it.
